<problem>
Identify Euclidean three-space with \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb C\). For distinct points \(Q_i=(\ell_i,\omega_i)\), \(1\le i\le n\), ordered by nondecreasing height \(\ell_i\), define, for \(i<j\),
\[
D_{ij}=\ell_j-\ell_i+\sqrt{(\ell_j-\ell_i)^2+|\omega_j-\omega_i|^2},
\qquad
f_{ij}(T)=1-\frac{\overline{\omega_j-\omega_i}}{D_{ij}}T,
\qquad
f_{ji}(T)=T+\frac{\omega_j-\omega_i}{D_{ij}}.
\]
Let
\[
P_i(T)=\prod_{j\ne i}f_{ij}(T),\qquad
M(Q)=\bigl([T^e]P_i(T)\bigr)_{1\le i\le n,\;0\le e<n},
\]
where \([T^e]\) denotes coefficient extraction. Call the configuration singular when \(\det M(Q)=0\), equivalently when these normalized Atiyah polynomials are linearly dependent over \(\mathbb C\).

For a positive integer \(m\), put \(\zeta_m=e^{2\pi i/m}\). Consider configurations consisting of
\[
\begin{aligned}
L_j&=(\lambda_j,0) &&(1\le j\le a),\\
A_k&=(h_-,r\zeta_m^k) &&(0\le k<m),\\
B_k&=(h_+,R\zeta_m^k) &&(0\le k<m),\\
U_j&=(\mu_j,0) &&(1\le j\le b),
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(a,b\ge1\) are integers, all heights are real, \(0<r<R\), and
\[
\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_a<h_-<h_+<\mu_1<\cdots<\mu_b.
\]
Order the points by the groups \(L,A,B,U\), with increasing indices within each group, so that \(n=a+b+2m\).

Determine exactly the set
\[
\mathscr S=\left\{m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:\ \text{for every integer }N\ge1\text{ there exists a singular configuration of the above form with }a+b+2m\ge N\right\}.
\]
</problem>

55	\[
56	P_A(T)=H_A(T)\bigl((T+x)(1+uT)\bigr)^K,

67	\[
68	H_A(t)>0,\qquad H_B(t)>0\qquad(0<t<1).

70	\]

120	\[
121	\lambda=-10,\quad h_-=0,\quad h_+=\frac1{1000},

159	## 3. The block is negative for large \(K\)
160	
161	For \(z=u,v\), construct a coefficient functional on polynomials in \(Z\). Its weights are
162	\[
163	w_j=z^{m(j-c)}\qquad(j\ge c),
164	\]
165	and, going backward, extend them by
166	\[
167	w_j=(x^m+y^m)w_{j+1}-(xy)^m w_{j+2}.
168	\tag{14}
169	\]
170	Call the resulting functional \(\mathcal L_z\).
171	
172	These functionals annihilate all axial rows (6)–(7). On the central columns \(Z^c,Z^{c+1}\), their matrix is
173	\[
174	\begin{pmatrix}1&u^m\\1&v^m\end{pmatrix}.
175	\]
176	Therefore, if \(A_K,B_K\) are the residue-\(0\) ring polynomials in \(Z\),
177	\[
178	\det
179	\begin{pmatrix}
180	\mathcal L_u(A_K)&\mathcal L_u(B_K)\\
181	\mathcal L_v(A_K)&\mathcal L_v(B_K)
182	\end{pmatrix}
183	=(v^m-u^m)\Delta_K.
184	\tag{15}
185	\]
186	The factor on the right is positive.
187	
188	We need the following elementary asymptotic fact.
189	
190	### Tail estimate
191	
192	Suppose
193	\[
194	P_K(T)=H(T)G(T)^K,\qquad G(T)=(T+\alpha)(1+\beta T),
195	\]
196	where \(H\) is fixed, \(H(z)>0\), and
197	\[
198	\beta z^2>\alpha.
199	\tag{16}
200	\]
201	Then the residue-\(0\) functional just constructed satisfies
202	\[
203	\mathcal L_z(P_K)
204	\sim \frac{H(z)}m\left(\frac{G(z)}z\right)^K.
205	\tag{17}
206	\]
207	Here the functional means application to the coefficients whose exponents are divisible by \(m\).
208	
209	To prove this, first observe that the backward solutions (14) are linear combinations of
210	\[
211	(x^m)^{c-j},\qquad (y^m)^{c-j}.
212	\]
213	Thus their absolute values for \(j<c\) are bounded independently of \(K\). Their difference from the geometric weights is consequently bounded by
214	\[
215	Cz^{m(j-c)}.
216	\tag{18}
217	\]
218	
219	Choose \(\tau<z\), sufficiently close to \(z\), such that
220	\[
221	\frac{G(\tau)}{\tau}<\frac{G(z)}z.
222	\tag{19}
223	\]
224	This is possible because
225	\[
226	\frac{G(t)}t=1+\alpha\beta+\beta t+\frac{\alpha}{t}
227	\]
228	is increasing when \(\beta t^2>\alpha\).
229	
230	Let \(\widehat H\) be obtained by taking absolute values of the coefficients of \(H\). The error arising from (18) is bounded by a constant times
231	\[
232	\sum_{e<K}|[T^e]P_K|z^{e-K}
233	\le
234	\widehat H(\tau)\left(\frac{G(\tau)}{\tau}\right)^K.
235	\tag{20}
236	\]
237	By (19), this is exponentially smaller than the proposed main term.
238	
239	Finally, the root-of-unity filter gives
240	\[
241	\sum_{m\mid e}[T^e]P_K\,z^e
242	=\frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}P_K(z\zeta_m^j).
243	\]
244	For \(j\ne0\),
245	\[
246	|G(z\zeta_m^j)|<G(z),
247	\]
248	because \(G\) has strictly positive constant, linear and quadratic coefficients. Hence its positive-real evaluation is the unique dominant term. This proves (17).
249	
250	Apply (17) to both ring rows and both \(z=u,v\). Conditions (16) follow from (11): it is enough to check the smaller value \(z=u\). Writing
251	\[
252	G_A(t)=(t+x)(1+ut),\qquad
253	G_B(t)=(t+y)(1+vt),
254	\]
255	we obtain
256	\[
257	\mathcal L_z(A_K)\sim
258	\frac{H_A(z)}m\left(\frac{G_A(z)}z\right)^K,
259	\]
260	\[
261	\mathcal L_z(B_K)\sim
262	\frac{H_B(z)}m\left(\frac{G_B(z)}z\right)^K.
263	\tag{21}
264	\]
265	All four main terms are positive. Moreover,
266	\[
267	\frac{\mathcal L_u(A_K)\mathcal L_v(B_K)}
268	{\mathcal L_u(B_K)\mathcal L_v(A_K)}
269	\sim
270	\frac{H_A(u)H_B(v)}{H_B(u)H_A(v)}
271	\left(\frac{\rho(u)}{\rho(v)}\right)^K
272	\longrightarrow0.
273	\]
274	Thus the determinant in (15) is negative for all sufficiently large multiples \(K\) of \(m\). Therefore
275	\[
276	\boxed{\Delta_K<0}
277	\tag{22}
278	\]
279	for all such \(K\).

281	## 4. A positive endpoint, then a genuine configuration
282	
283	Keep the heights (9), and scale both radii by \(\varepsilon>0\). For a fixed \(K\) satisfying (22), let the corresponding block determinant be \(\Delta_K(\varepsilon)\).
284

286	\[
287	x,y,u,v\to0,\qquad C_m(T)\to1,\qquad E_m(T)\to T^m.
288	\]
289	The two base ring rows consequently tend to
290	\[
291	T^K F_m(T),\qquad T^{K+m}F_m(T).
292	\]
293	Since \(\deg F_m=m-1\) and \(F_m(0)=1\), their residue-\(0\) components are simply
294	\[
295	T^K,\qquad T^{K+m}.
296	\]
297	The axial rows tend to the other coordinate monomials. Hence
298	\[
299	\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\Delta_K(\varepsilon)=1.
300	\tag{23}
301	\]
302	Choose \(\varepsilon_0>0\) small enough that
303	\[
304	\Delta_K(\varepsilon_0)>0,\qquad \Delta_K(1)<0.
305	\tag{24}
306	\]
307

309	\[
310	\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_K
311	\]
312	sufficiently close to \(-10\), and strictly increasing heights

314	\mu_1<\cdots<\mu_K

316	sufficiently close to \(1/10\). They can be chosen so that all required height inequalities hold and both strict signs in (24) persist.

320	\varepsilon_*\in(\varepsilon_0,1).
321	\]
322	By (8), this is a singular configuration. Its radii satisfy
323	\[
324	0<\varepsilon_*<10\varepsilon_*,
325	\]

328	n=2K+2m.
329	\]

mp.mp.dps=120
K=150
N=2*K+2
q=[(mp.mpf(-10)+mp.mpf('1e-10')*j,mp.mpf(0)) for j in range(K)]
q += [(mp.mpf(0),mp.mpf(1)),(mp.mpf('0.001'),mp.mpf(10))]
q += [(mp.mpf('0.1')+mp.mpf('1e-10')*j,mp.mpf(0)) for j in range(K)]
M=mp.matrix(N,N)
for i in range(N):
 p=[mp.mpf(1)]
 shift=0
 for j in range(N):
  if j==i: continue
  lo,hi=min(i,j),max(i,j)
  dh=q[hi][0]-q[lo][0]
  dw=q[hi][1]-q[lo][1]
  D=dh+mp.sqrt(dh*dh+dw*dw)
  if i<j:
   a,b=mp.mpf(1),-dw/D

  if b==0: continue
  if a==0: shift+=1;continue
  new=[mp.mpf(0)]*(len(p)+1)
  for e,c in enumerate(p):
   new[e]+=a*c
   new[e+1]+=b*c
  p=new
 for e,c in enumerate(p): M[i,e+shift]=c
val=mp.det(M)
print('Strict distinct original-definition matrix determinant:',mp.nstr(val,50))
assert val<0
